slot.brief: Blocks in contact or connected by string on frictionless surface; find acceleration then contact/tension force

stem: Two blocks of masses $4\ \text{kg}$ and $6\ \text{kg}$ are in contact on a frictionless horizontal surface. A horizontal force of $20\ \text{N}$ is applied to the $4\ \text{kg}$ block towards the $6\ \text{kg}$ block. The magnitude of the contact force between the two blocks is:

verdicts.working: a = F/(m1+m2) = 20/10 = 2 m/s². Contact force = m2·a = 6×2 = 12 N (check: 20 − 4×2 = 12 N).

working:
Step 1: Treat both blocks as a single system to find their common acceleration.
$$a = \dfrac{F}{m_1 + m_2} = \dfrac{20\ \text{N}}{4\ \text{kg} + 6\ \text{kg}} = \dfrac{20}{10} = 2\ \text{m s}^{-2}$$

Step 2: Isolate the $6\ \text{kg}$ block. The only horizontal force acting on it is the normal contact force $N$ exerted by the $4\ \text{kg}$ block.
$$N = m_2 a = 6\ \text{kg} \times 2\ \text{m s}^{-2} = 12\ \text{N}$$

Thus, the contact force between the blocks is $12\ \text{N}$.

Independent check: a = F/(m1+m2) = 20/10 = 2 m/s². Contact force = m2·a = 6×2 = 12 N (check: 20 − 4×2 = 12 N).

draft.distractor_notes:
$8\ \text{N}$ comes from calculating $m_1 a = 4 \times 2\ \text{N}$, which would be the contact force if the force were applied to the $6\ \text{kg}$ block instead.
$10\ \text{N}$ comes from naively assuming the force splits equally between the two blocks ($F/2$).
$20\ \text{N}$ comes from assuming the entire external force is transmitted across the contact interface.
